chronoseries_scale_neighbours.note: The Cavia chronoseries has a single Holocene node (0 Ma). Neighbours below are the adjacent size tiers at the same age, not other chronospecies.
chronoseries_scale_neighbours.predecessor_relation: One 1267 µm flank-envelope wavelength contains exactly 10 s0 waves of 126.7 µm. On a 1.0136 mm primordium the predecessor mode is unresolved.
chronoseries_scale_neighbours.successor_relation: Ten 12.67 µm successor waves fit inside one s0 wavelength and are coarse-grained out of the Swift-Hohenberg equation.

state_variables.role: Swift-Hohenberg real amplitude of the critical Turing mode

boundary_conditions: Periodic on a square primordium of side 8 * 126.7 µm = 1013.6 µm. No-flux skin edges are not resolved; the window is an interior patch of dermis.

equations.schnakenberg: du/dt = D_u laplacian(u) + gamma (a - u + u^2 v); dv/dt = D_v laplacian(v) + gamma (b - u^2 v)
equations.turing_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v); lambda_c = 2 pi / k_c
equations.swift_hohenberg: dA/dt = epsilon A - (k_c^2 + laplacian)^2 A - A^3

parameters.note: D_u and D_v are derived in the script so that lambda_c is exactly 126.7 µm. They are intentionally not the Murray textbook (a, b, d) = (0.1, 0.9, 10) set used by other slots.

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) showed a homogeneous chemical steady state can be unstable to a finite band of wavenumbers when the inhibitor diffuses farther than the activator.
Murray (1981) identified that selected wavelength with mammalian coat prepatterns (stripes, spots).
Sick et al. (2006) showed a WNT/DKK reaction-diffusion interaction sets mammalian hair-follicle spacing, the anatomical neighbour of a ~100 µm pigment wavelength.

The 126.7 µm figure is the slot-assigned tier-5 detail length for extant Cavia porcellus (0.0001267 m). It is not a published guinea-pig histology measurement, and the script does not claim that it is.
